inlines.text: 世界动作模型让机器人自主性更上一层楼

blocks.text: 更高水平的机器人自主性要求机器人感知周围环境、预判自身动作将如何改变环境，并以高精度执行复杂的多步骤任务。世界动作模型正是为此而生。

inlines.text: 更高水平的机器人自主性要求机器人感知周围环境、预判自身动作将如何改变环境，并以高精度执行复杂的多步骤任务。世界动作模型正是为此而生。

blocks.text: 在 CoRL 上，NVIDIA 将推出 GR00T 2，这是一个基于 NVIDIA Cosmos 构建的开放前沿世界动作模型。该模型在多样化的机器人和人类数据上训练，包括 100,000 小时的 NVIDIA 开源人类第一人称视角数据，使机器人能够学习灵巧操作技能。主要特性包括：

inlines.text: 在 CoRL 上，NVIDIA 将推出
GR00T 2
，这是一个基于 NVIDIA Cosmos 构建的开放前沿世界动作模型。该模型在多样化的机器人和人类数据上训练，包括 100,000 小时的
NVIDIA 开源人类第一人称视角数据
，使机器人能够学习灵巧操作技能。主要特性包括：
开箱即用的表现：
在没有针对具体任务的演示的情况下，50 项评估任务中至少有 40 项完成过一次。
技能迁移：
从人类演示中学习，并在没有机器人演示的情况下，将技能迁移到不同的机器人本体上。
小数据泛化：
每个任务仅需一次演示，就能在 50 个任务上取得平均 71% 的成功率；演示增加到五次后，成功率提升至 95%。
智能体控制：
AI 智能体可以调用 GR00T 2 的应用程序接口和配套工具，按顺序执行各项技能，并在出错后恢复。

blocks.text: NVIDIA Isaac Lab 是一个开源机器人学习框架，为这项工作提供了基础。其最新版本 Isaac Lab 3.0 让研究人员可以借助智能体，利用可直接用于仿真的资产快速搭建训练环境，在 NVIDIA PhysX 与 Newton 物理求解器之间切换，为基于感知的训练选择渲染器，并对 GR00T 等基础模型应用新的强化学习后训练库。

blocks.text: AlphaNIST 基于 Isaac Lab 构建，展示了高效练习如何转化为精准操作。单一策略即可学会 NIST 装配任务板上的全部 20 项任务，仅凭“成功/失败”的二值信号就能操作毫米级零件。其训练成功率超过 98%，而按任务分别训练的策略为 81%，且 GPU 时间约减少 39 倍。

blocks.text: NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena 是一个用于规模化策略评估的开源框架，开发者可以用它组合出多样且可重复的评估，再并行地在数千种变体上运行策略。分析结果能揭示哪些条件会导致失败，让研究人员知道下一轮训练该修什么。其最新版本 0.4 的开发者预览版将在 CoRL 上发布。

blocks.text: The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems.

blocks.text: Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL:

inlines.text: Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL:
GRAIL
(Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning.
RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies

blocks.text: World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy

inlines.text: World Action Models Enable Next Level of Robot Autonomy

blocks.text: The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that.

inlines.text: The next level of robot autonomy requires robots to perceive their surroundings, anticipate how their actions will change the environment and execute complex, multistep tasks with a high degree of precision. World action models enable exactly that.

blocks.text: At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing GR00T 2, an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of NVIDIA open source human egocentric data, the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include:

inlines.text: At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing
GR00T 2
, an open frontier world action model built on NVIDIA Cosmos. Trained on diverse robot and human data, including 100,000 hours of
NVIDIA open source human egocentric data
, the model enables robots to learn dexterous manipulation skills. Key features include:
Out-of-the-box performance:
Completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks at least once without task-specific demonstrations.
Skill transfer:
Learns from human demonstrations and transfers skills between different robot bodies without robot demonstrations
Generalization with little data:
Achieved 71% average success across 50 tasks with just one demonstration per task, increasing to 95% with five.
Agent control:
AI agents can use GR00T 2’s application programming interface and supporting tools to run skills in sequence and recover from errors.

blocks.text: GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins.

inlines.text: GR00T 2 currently ranks among the top three models across all vision language action and world action model categories for the RoboCasa365, RoboLab, RoboDojo and MolmoSpaces benchmarks, with multiple leaderboard wins.

blocks.text: Nexuni is testing it for robotic laundry handling, Foxconn is applying GR00T 2 to factory automation for server manufacturing and Siemens is evaluating it across industrial use cases.

blocks.text: MicroAGI is using GR00T 2, post-trained through reinforcement learning, to perform Ethernet cable swapping with a YAM robotic arm. Its agentic robotics approach automates the creation and calibration of simulation environments using Isaac Lab 3.0 and Newton, where the policy is trained.

blocks.text: Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation

inlines.text: Where the Training and Scaling Happens — in Simulation

blocks.text: A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots.

inlines.text: A pretrained model gives robots a core set of skills. Simulation lets researchers train, refine and evaluate skills at scale before deploying them on physical robots.

blocks.text: NVIDIA Isaac Lab, an open source robot-learning framework, provides the foundation for that work. Its latest release, Isaac Lab 3.0, allows researchers to use agents to quickly set up training environments with simulation-ready assets, switch between NVIDIA PhysX and Newton physics solvers, choose renderers for perception-based training and apply a new reinforcement post-training library to foundation models like GR00T.

blocks.text: Accurate physics is critical to transferring learned skills from simulation to the real robot. Tighter integration with Newton, an open source physics engine, now allows Isaac Lab to model deformable objects such as cables and cloth, along with complex articulated systems such as robotic hands with many interacting joints.

blocks.text: Together, Isaac Lab and Newton combine accurate physics with scale to enable researchers to train thousands of simulated robots in parallel. In a vision-based dexterous manipulation benchmark, Isaac Lab 3.0 with Newton achieved up to 2.5x the training throughput of Isaac Lab 2.3 with PhysX.

blocks.text: AlphaNIST, built in Isaac Lab, demonstrates how efficient practice can translate into precision. A single policy learns all 20 tasks on the NIST Assembly Task Board, manipulating millimeter-scale parts using only a yes-or-no success signal. It achieves more than 98% training success, compared with 81% for separate per-task policies, using roughly 39x less GPU time.

blocks.text: Behind those results is Success-Guided Sampling, or SGS, from the University of Washington and NVIDIA. The method focuses practice on tasks a policy succeeds at about half the time, directing training toward skills it’s still learning. With SGS, robot training can scale beyond a million parallel environments.

blocks.text: New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation

inlines.text: New Industrial Benchmarks for Robot Evaluation

blocks.text: Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another.

inlines.text: Learning a skill is one challenge. Performing it reliably across changing conditions is another.

blocks.text: NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, an open source framework for scaled policy evaluation, enables developers to compose diverse and repeatable evaluations, then run policies across thousands of variations in parallel. Analyses expose which conditions cause failures, so researchers know what to fix in their next training run. The developer preview of its latest version, 0.4, is arriving at CoRL.

blocks.text: DexBench and VABAR, two new open benchmarks, are among the first designed to measure robot dexterity and adaptability across industrial tasks using Isaac Lab-Arena and Newton.

blocks.text: DexBench, developed by RLWRLD in collaboration with NVIDIA, takes dexterity evaluation off the tabletop and into real-world workflows. Built using NVIDIA Isaac Lab-Arena, it features 15 tasks across four scenes spanning retail, logistics, manufacturing and hospitality, testing generalization across object, spatial and physics variations.

blocks.text: Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs

inlines.text: Agents Turn Skills Into Robot Programs

blocks.text: Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge.

inlines.text: Successful task completion requires robots to coordinate multiple skills and adapt when something goes wrong. Building reliable programs for these multistep tasks remains a challenge.

blocks.text: Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge.

inlines.text: Agentic robotics helps solve that challenge.

blocks.text: UC Berkeley’s new Graph-as-Policy (GaP) framework uses agents to connect individual skills into robot programs. Agents test these programs using NVIDIA Isaac open simulation technologies and refine them based on failures. This helps researchers scale development with less data while keeping the programs interpretable for engineers to review and verify before deployment.
